title: Presidential Determination Pursuant to Section 101 of the Defense Production Act of 1950, as Amended, on Recoverable Critical Minerals and Materials
key_claim: The 30 July 2026 determination finds recoverable critical minerals and materials, defined to include black mass, end-of-life rare-earth permanent magnets and other waste and scrap containing them, essential to national defence, and directs Commerce to act under Section 101 of the Defense Production Act; copper scrap is excluded because Proclamation 10962 already covers it.
frame_summary: The White House treats recycling-stream materials as defence industrial inputs whose supply must be secured by Defense Production Act action rather than left to the market.
verbatim_quote: It is imperative that the United States takes immediate action to secure the supply of recoverable CMMs.
verbatim_list: does not include copper scrap, which is already covered under Proclamation 10962 of July 30, 2025
includes black mass, end-of-life, rare-earth permanent magnets or other goods that have fully completed the manufacturing

title: DPAS Directive Allocation Order and Additional Requirements for Recoverable Critical Minerals and Materials (temporary final rule, FR Doc. 2026-16078)
key_claim: BIS's temporary final rule requires US sellers of black mass and tungsten waste and scrap to allocate 100% of monthly sales to US persons absent a BIS exception or adjustment, takes effect 21 days after publication, ceases 386 days after publication, and lets Customs detain covered exports during BIS review.
frame_summary: Commerce converts the defence determination into a domestic-first sales mandate on two recycling-stream materials, with case-by-case exceptions as the only route abroad.
verbatim_quote: must allocate 100 percent of monthly sales to U.S. persons
verbatim_list: expire one year from its effective date
posing an imminent threat to U.S. military readiness and critical infrastructure sectors
Any covered materials intended for export may be detained by CBP while BIS conducts its review of the shipment.
notes: WebFetch 21/10/2026 of the Federal Register public-inspection PDF. The effective date (27 August 2026) and the end date (about 27 August 2027, 386 days after publication) are the analyst's calculation from the rule's relative dates; Steptoe and Beveridge & Diamond (not cited) state 27 August 2026 as the effective date.

title: Commission publishes draft list of countries authorised to import EU waste
key_claim: The Commission published on 18 September 2026 a draft list of non-OECD countries that could be authorised to import non-hazardous EU waste after 21 May 2027; 32 countries asked to keep receiving it; feedback is open to 16 October; the first list is due by the end of 2026.
frame_summary: The Commission frames the export curb as environmental-soundness waste law, with a default of no exports to non-OECD countries and listed exceptions.
verbatim_quote: As a general principle, the EU will no longer export waste to non-OECD countries from 21 May 2027.
verbatim_list: 32 countries submitted such requests to the Commission.
notes: WebFetch 21/10/2026; the fetch tool paraphrased parts of the page and returned the two quoted sentences as page text; confirmed by hand against that output.

title: Global Critical Minerals Outlook 2026: Executive summary
key_claim: Under current policies average recycling rates across key energy minerals could rise from around 10% today to close to 20% by 2040; China holds over three-quarters of global battery pre-treatment capacity and 90% of material recovery capacity; the expanded Chinese rare earth measures were suspended until November 2026.
frame_summary: The IEA presents recycling as a growing but concentrated supply source, with processing capacity held overwhelmingly in China.

verbatim_list: China accounting for over three-quarters of global pre-treatment capacity and 90% of material recovery capacity
Although the expanded measures were suspended for one year until November 2026
secondary supply potentially doubling its contribution by 2040

title: US black mass export restrictions could bolster domestic refiners
key_claim: Benchmark analyst Frederick Bloomfield expects the black mass export ban to redirect feedstock towards US recyclers, and says the key question is whether it accelerates US black mass refining build-out.
frame_summary: Benchmark reads the US order as a feedstock-redirection measure whose success depends on whether domestic refining capacity follows.
verbatim_quote: A ban on the export of black mass should redirect feedstock towards US recyclers.
verbatim_list: The key question is whether the policy will accelerate the buildout of US black mass refining capacity.

title: European recyclers to fight proposed EU metal waste export ban: CMA
key_claim: The Circular Metal Association says the Commission applies a stricter standard to recycled metals than to other waste; S&P reports the proposal would cut aluminium scrap exports by 76% (970,600 t) and steel scrap exports by 25%-26% (4 million-4.1 million t), from 21 May 2027.
frame_summary: S&P frames the draft list as a metal-specific restriction that European recyclers say prejudges a whole material group and will strand surpluses.
verbatim_quote: the Commission applies a significantly stricter standard to recycled metals than to other types of waste
verbatim_list: reduce EU annual exports of steel scrap by 4 million-4.1 million metric tons, or 25%-26%
sales markets will disappear, material values will come under pressure and surpluses will grow
notes: WebFetch 21/10/2026; byline Katya Bouckley, Platts. The 76% and 970,600 t figures are as reported by S&P, not published in a Commission document.

title: EU shifts aluminium scrap export policy away from planned trade measures
key_claim: The Commission withdrew a planned trade instrument on aluminium scrap exports and is working instead on a delegated act under the Waste Shipments Regulation, expected to be adopted by the end of 2026.
frame_summary: Fastmarkets reports the EU moving the aluminium scrap fix from a trade measure to waste-shipment law because the first design would have covered only about half of exports.
verbatim_quote: The European Commission has withdrawn a planned trade instrument
notes: WebFetch 21/10/2026; byline Declan Conway. Fastmarkets attributes the account to a statement from Executive Vice-President Stephane Sejourne's cabinet reported by Reuters; the Commission had not yet confirmed it when the article ran.

title: EU publishes draft list of countries authorized to import EU waste
key_claim: Under the draft list, metal waste exports would be authorised only to Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine; India is approved for other streams but not metal waste; the first list is due by 21 November 2026.
frame_summary: SteelOrbis reports the draft list as sharply narrowing the legal destinations for EU metal scrap.
verbatim_quote: metal waste exports would be authorized to Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine
verbatim_list: India was approved in the draft for several other waste streams covered by its application, but not for metal waste.
The first list is due to be established by November 21, 2026.
